what_this_is: JudgeEscrowV2 on Base Sepolia: an escrow a PANEL settles rather than a single finalizer key. The panel is committed at job creation and nothing moves until a quorum of its members signs.
proven_on_chain: one member's signature is refused on a 3-of-5
three distinct committed members record the verdict
what_changed_from_v1: V1 consumes ONE finalizer signature. A 5-of-9 panel decision was recorded by nine people and executed by one key: the receipt proved a quorum agreed, and the escrow could not tell whether it had. V2 checks the signatures against the panel the AGREEMENT named, not against the platform's finalizer registry, because a panel is whoever the two parties chose.
why_the_panel_is_committed: keccak256(quorum, sortedMembers) is stored at creation. Without it a caller could supply a panel of their own choosing — every signature would verify against it perfectly, and the settlement would be authorised by people the agreement never named.
v1_still_works: Jobs created with no panel commitment take the single-finalizer path unchanged, so V1 behaviour is preserved rather than deprecated by fiat. The two paths refuse each other explicitly.
